metadata.title: The Quantum Future of Finance Applications: Challenges and Strategic Opportunities
metadata.venue: Book chapter in Emerging Trends and Innovations in Financial Services: A Futurology Perspective (IGI Global Scientific Publishing)

problem_domains.description: Use of quantum computing to improve financial forecasting and predictive analytics.
problem_domains.quote: It has the promise of accessing the Power of Quantum Computing for Enhanced Forecasting, Portfolio Optimization, etc.

problem_domains.description: Detecting anomalous or fraudulent financial transactions with fewer false positives.
problem_domains.quote: Likewise, the exponential acceleration of computation promised by quantum computers has potential benefits in fraud detection (Zhou, 2025). For instance, quantum- enabled anomaly detection which enables the identification of anomalous transaction patterns in real- time, could possibly lower false positives and improve the efficacy of fraud prevention when monitoring credit card and other banking transactions.

problem_domains.description: Assessing financial risk, including complex derivatives and systemic risk, via simulations and models.
problem_domains.quote: For instance, quantum algorithms like the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) are designed to resolve problems that would need days of pro- cessing on traditional computers, for example, risk assessment, derivative pricing, and portfolio optimization (Zhou, 2025).
problem_domains.location: Section 1.1 Why do we want to use quantum computing in finance? / Page 3

problem_domains.description: Pricing derivatives whose value depends on underlying assets modeled by stochastic processes.

problem_domains.description: Solving complex problems in strategic planning and key decision-making for financial institutions.
problem_domains.quote: Since quantum computing has the ability to solve complex problems faster and with greater accuracy, it can potentially revolutionize strategic planning and key decision- making.
problem_domains.location: Introduction / Page 2

problem_domains.problem: Financial modeling, supply chain optimization, and simulation
problem_domains.description: Using quantum computing to gain competitive advantage in financial modeling and related optimization/simulation tasks.
problem_domains.quote: This brings significant competitive advantages for those willing to leverage its power in areas such as financial modeling, supply chain optimization, and simulation.
problem_domains.location: Section 1.1 Why do we want to use quantum computing in finance? / Page 3

problem_domains.description: Transforming how banks recognize, minimize, and report risks across departments.
problem_domains.quote: With quantum computing, risk- related regulatory reporting will be transformed.
problem_domains.location: Section 2.2 Threat and Cybersecurity / Page 6

problem_domains.description: Improving fraud detection for new payment schemes and transactions.
problem_domains.quote: For detecting fraud, new payment schemes and transactions can minimize episodes. Although professionals now believe that quantum computing is only marginally able to enhance rule- based fraud detection, employing additional variables will be able to make fraud- detection algorithms more precise.
problem_domains.location: Section 2.2 Threat and Cybersecurity / Page 6

problem_domains.problem: Portfolio creation and risk assessment in investment banking
problem_domains.description: Balancing returns and variance in increasingly complex portfolios.
problem_domains.quote: Portfolio creation and risk assessment are some of the areas being re- designed in the ever- changing investment banking landscape by quantum computing.
problem_domains.location: Section 2.2 Threat and Cybersecurity / Page 6

problem_domains.description: Improving precision of credit decisions for retail banking customers.
problem_domains.quote: Two of the most important applications are credit- decision software and collateral optimization, both of which might be better with greater precision.
problem_domains.location: Section 2.3 Retail Banking / Page 6–7

problem_domains.description: Optimizing collateral under additional values and data types as constraints.
problem_domains.quote: The second may introduce additional values and data types as constraints of the optimization problem.
problem_domains.location: Section 2.3 Retail Banking / Page 7

problem_domains.description: Addressing money laundering issues in blockchain-based payment systems.
problem_domains.quote: Especially, quantum payments would be able to solve the existing issue of money laundering on the blockchain (Dey et al., 2022).
problem_domains.location: Section 2.4 Payments / Page 7

problem_domains.problem: Security of inter and intra bank communication
problem_domains.description: Ensuring future inter- and intra-bank security for payments and communication.
problem_domains.quote: The future of the inter and intra bank security would be quantum money operat- ing with the QKD protocols.
problem_domains.location: Section 2.4 Payments / Page 7

problem_domains.problem: Derivatives pricing and portfolio optimization in investment banking
problem_domains.description: Improving derivatives pricing and portfolio optimization using detailed digital representations of banks.
problem_domains.quote: Quantum computing would find application in investment banking, where it would be able to facilitate the much- desired improvement in the derivatives pricing and portfolio optimization.
problem_domains.location: Section 2.5 Investment Banking / Page 7–8

problem_domains.description: Solving complex optimization problems and simultaneous arbitrage across markets under tight time constraints.
problem_domains.quote: These complicated optimization problems can be challenging to find the solution within computational time when determining simultaneous arbitrage across two or more markets.
problem_domains.location: Section 5. HFT AND QUANTUM ALGORITHMS / Page 11

problem_domains.problem: Secure communication and cryptography for financial data
problem_domains.description: Protecting sensitive financial communications and data from eavesdropping and future quantum attacks.
problem_domains.quote: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is a secure communication method that uses the principles of quantum mechanics to derive and share a secret cryptographic key between two parties, assuring that any attempt to eavesdrop will be detectable immediately. Financial institutions are exploring and piloting QKD for its potential as a critical layer in the quantum- safe security paradigm.
problem_domains.location: Section 3. QUANTUM KEY DISTRIBUTION / Page 9

problem_domains.description: Securing data center interconnects and disaster recovery links in financial networks.
problem_domains.quote: Financial institutions are utilizing quantum key distribution (QKD) to provide enhanced protection for their most mission- critical high- bandwidth communication links.
problem_domains.location: Section 3. QUANTUM KEY DISTRIBUTION – Execution in Financial Networks / Page 9

problem_domains.problem: Derivative pricing via Monte Carlo-style simulations
problem_domains.description: Pricing derivatives using Monte Carlo-style simulations over stochastic processes.
problem_domains.quote: In finance, one important asset- pricing problem is the pricing of derivatives.
problem_domains.location: Section 3.1 Quantum techniques for Monte Carlo- style Derivative Pricing and Risk Management / Page 9

problem_domains.description: Improving speed and accuracy of risk simulations such as Monte Carlo analysis.
problem_domains.quote: Nowadays, banks calculate risk by complex simulations, such as Monte Carlo analysis, with the support of conventional supercomputers.
problem_domains.location: Section 4.1 Extremely Accurate Risk Simulation / Page 10

problem_domains.description: Making credit scoring more fair and accurate and expanding credit access.
problem_domains.quote: This could create a more fair and accurate credit scoring that can result in credit becoming available to many more people.
problem_domains.location: Section 4.2 Improved Fraud Detection and Credit Scoring / Page 10

problem_domains.description: Finding optimal asset combinations under exponentially growing combinations and risk.
problem_domains.quote: The number of assets and the number of combinations in which the optimal combination of asset can be maximized to give maximum possible returns grows exponentially with the amount of risk.
problem_domains.location: Section 4.3 Asset Allocation Optimization / Page 10–11

problem_domains.problem: Pricing and portfolio optimization for net zero and climate-related risk
problem_domains.description: Using quantum computing for pricing, portfolio optimization, and managing climate-related and fraud risks.
problem_domains.quote: HSBC are utilizing quantum computing for pricing and portfolio optimization, to further their net zero ambitions, and to manage risk including identifying and acting against fraudulent activity.
problem_domains.location: Section 6. QUANTUM IN CENTRAL BANKING AND MONETARY POLICY / Page 11–12

problem_domains.description: Improving financial forecasting and churn prediction using quantum-inspired and quantum ML.
problem_domains.quote: First, we apply the classical and quantum Determinantal Point Process to improve Random Forest models to predict churn, with improvements in precision of nearly 6%.
problem_domains.location: Section 6.1 Quantum and Machine Learning for Finance / Page 12

problem_domains.description: Assessing credit risk with more efficient models using quantum neural networks.
problem_domains.quote: Second, we develop quantum neural network architectures that use orthogonal and compound layers for credit risk assessment, matching classical performance with significantly fewer parameters.

problem_domains.description: Enhancing risk assessment models for improved financial stability.
problem_domains.quote: Risk Assessment: QML could enhance risk assessment models, resulting in improved financial stability and a more accurate evaluation of risk.

problem_domains.description: Improving fraud detection by enhancing pattern recognition to identify new financial crimes.
problem_domains.quote: Fraud Detection: QML improves fraud detection processes by enhancing pattern recognition capabilities to identify newer ways to commit financial crime.

problem_domains.description: Developing and optimizing trading strategies using QML.
problem_domains.quote: Trading Strategies: It can improve the development and optimization of trading strategies.

problem_domains.description: Providing more accurate pricing models for financial derivatives via quantum Monte Carlo.
problem_domains.quote: Derivative Pricing: QML would provide pricing models for financial derivatives that are more accurate by modeling market behavior more accurately by using methods like quantum Monte Carlo simulations.
problem_domains.location: Section 6.1 Quantum and Machine Learning for Finance / Page 12

problem_domains.problem: Credit scoring optimization via quantum annealer
problem_domains.description: Optimizing the credit scoring process using a quantum annealer.
problem_domains.quote: Credit scoring: By using a quantum annealer (a type of quantum computer), the credit scoring process could be optimized.
problem_domains.location: Section 6.1 Quantum and Machine Learning for Finance / Page 12–13

problem_domains.description: Developing encryption methods safe against future quantum computation.
problem_domains.quote: Post- Quantum Cryptography. Quantum computing is critical for developing methods of encryption that are safe against future quantum computation in order to protect financial data (Shor, 1997).
problem_domains.location: Section 6.2 Quantum Computing in Finance / Page 13

problem_domains.problem: Fraud detection and quantum resistant infrastructure
problem_domains.description: Using quantum solutions for fraud detection and building quantum-resistant infrastructure.
problem_domains.quote: Banks like HSBC, Santander, and Yapili Kredi are also using quantum solutions to do various tasks including fraud detection and quantum resistant infrastructure.
problem_domains.location: Section 7. THE QUANTUM LEAP / Page 14

problem_domains.problem: Protecting trading information in FX trading
problem_domains.description: Safeguarding highly sensitive foreign exchange trading information from future quantum attacks.
problem_domains.quote: HSBC is the first bank offering quantum security in the AI- driven foreign ex- change trading. At the forefront of exploring how quantum cryptography can safe- guard highly sensitive trading information from prospective cyber risks as powerful as future quantum attacks is HSBC, a global top- tier foreign exchange provider.
problem_domains.location: Section 7. THE QUANTUM LEAP / Page 14

problem_domains.problem: More accurate risk modeling, fraud prevention, and portfolio optimization
problem_domains.description: Improving risk models, fraud prevention, and portfolio optimization via cutting-edge technology.
problem_domains.quote: •  More accurate risk modeling, fraud prevention, and portfolio optimization are all facilitated by quantum computing.
problem_domains.location: Section 8. THREE STRATEGIES FOR BANKS TO USE CUTTING- EDGE TECHNOLOGY IN FINANCIAL SERVICES / Page 15

problem_domains.description: Improving synchronization of high-frequency trading algorithms via precise measurements.
problem_domains.quote: •  Synchronization of high- frequency trading (HFT) algorithms could be im- proved by quantum sensing's capacity to provide accurate measurements.
problem_domains.location: Section 8. THREE STRATEGIES FOR BANKS TO USE CUTTING- EDGE TECHNOLOGY IN FINANCIAL SERVICES / Page 15

problem_domains.problem: Valuation modeling in M&A and deal structuring
problem_domains.description: Running many market scenarios quickly to value deals more precisely.
problem_domains.quote: Its applications in the field of valuation modeling are perhaps most impressive. By enabling the running of many different market scenarios within a relatively short time, quantum systems enable a higher degree of precision that was hitherto unimaginable with traditional methods.
problem_domains.location: Section 8.1 Restructuring of Acquisitions, Deals and Mergers / Page 15–16

problem_domains.description: Quantum computers threatening current cryptography that secures financial data and digital currencies.
problem_domains.quote: The most pressing and urgent one is the threat to existing cryptographic systems posed by quantum computers.
problem_domains.location: Section 9.1 The Emergence of Quantum- Resistant Security / Page 18

problem_domains.description: Migrating financial sector cryptography to PQC to secure sensitive information.
problem_domains.quote: The financial sector needs to transition to post- quantum cryptography (PQC) standards to secure sensitive information from prospective quantum attacks.
problem_domains.location: Section 9.1 The Emergence of Quantum- Resistant Security / Page 18

problem_domains.problem: Real-time capital flow and dynamic collateral management
problem_domains.description: Building a new infrastructure layer enabling real-time capital flow and dynamic collateral management.
problem_domains.quote: Quantum technology might also be a new financial infrastructure layer in the long- term, with real- time capital flow, dynamic collateral management, and secure inter- bank communication via quantum networking and key distribution (QKD) (Zhou, 2025)
problem_domains.location: Section 10. A NEW LAYER OF FINANCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE / Page 18

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum-enabled anomaly detection
solution_approaches.description: Using quantum computing to detect anomalous transaction patterns in real time for fraud detection.
solution_approaches.quote: For instance, quantum- enabled anomaly detection which enables the identification of anomalous transaction patterns in real- time, could possibly lower false positives and improve the efficacy of fraud prevention when monitoring credit card and other banking transactions.

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum parallelism and interference for portfolio creation
solution_approaches.description: Using quantum parallelism and interference to evaluate enormous sets of asset combinations simultaneously.
solution_approaches.quote: Applying quantum parallelism and interference, they can make calculations over an impossibly enormous set of combinations of assets at the same time, weighting their calculations toward their most optimal outcomes.
solution_approaches.location: Section 2.2 Threat and Cybersecurity / Page 6

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum computing for real-time decision-making in corporate banking
solution_approaches.description: Leveraging quantum computing to facilitate critical and automated decisions in real time.
solution_approaches.quote: Quantum computing facilitates making critical decisions and even automated decision- making in real- time (Ghosh, 2024).
solution_approaches.location: Section 2.1 Corporate Banking / Page 5

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum machine learning for risk simulation
solution_approaches.description: Using quantum machine learning to simulate risks considering broader sets of variables and assets.
solution_approaches.quote: Quantum machine learning can enable decision makers to take into account a broader set of variables and assets when it comes to simulating risks (Patel, 2025).
solution_approaches.location: Section 2.2 Threat and Cybersecurity / Page 6

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum payments and quantum money with QKD
solution_approaches.description: Implementing quantum states as money and using QKD protocols for secure payments.
solution_approaches.quote: Quantum states are true non falsifiable money because they cannot be replicated. One of the significant factors that we anticipate will enable quantum payments is the hardware required for quantum key distribution (QKD).
solution_approaches.location: Section 2.5 Payments / Page 7

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum Monte Carlo algorithms
solution_approaches.description: Using quantum Monte Carlo algorithms to enhance simulations such as those used in derivatives pricing and settlement.
solution_approaches.quote: In the long run, banks could for instance adopt quantum Monte Carlo algorithms (as a case in point), build on their existing classical means, and this means may already be commercially pre- existing as far as insti- tutional settlement in the future through well established smart contracts
solution_approaches.location: Section 2.5 Investment Banking / Page 8

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum random number generation (QRNG)

solution_approaches.location: Section 8. THREE STRATEGIES FOR BANKS TO USE CUTTING- EDGE TECHNOLOGY IN FINANCIAL SERVICES / Page 15

solution_approaches.approach: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD)

solution_approaches.approach: Hybrid QKD and Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC)
solution_approaches.description: Combining QKD with PQC as a hybrid quantum-safe security strategy.

solution_approaches.location: Section 3. QUANTUM KEY DISTRIBUTION – Execution in Financial Networks / Page 9

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing is a developing technology that can potentially revolutionize the financial services industry.
